mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome—I'm so glad you're here for this journey. Have you ever wondered what it really means to follow a higher calling—even when it asks a lot from you? There's a certain power in teachings that don't just comfort us, but actually challenge us to go deeper, to commit with our whole selves. That's exactly where The Cost of Discipleship by Dietrich Bonhoeffer comes in. Together, we're going to explore the tension between grace and obedience, and what it looks like to let faith shape every part of our lives—not just on the surface, but deep down, where real transformation happens. Bonhoeffer wrote out of a world facing moral crisis, where standing up for what’s right wasn't just difficult—it was dangerous. He invites us to look honestly at the difference between “cheap” grace—the kind that asks nothing of us—and “costly” grace, which can demand everything. So, what does it actually mean to answer that invitation? We'll walk through the teachings of the Sermon on the Mount, and see how the call to follow isn’t just about believing, but about living and acting in new ways—ways that might cost us, but also set us free. As we move forward together, let's stay open to the possibility that discipleship isn’t a burden to bear, but a path toward true purpose, fulfillment, and freedom. Are you ready to discover the real meaning—and the real cost—of living a life shaped by faith? Let’s dive in and find out together.
